findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. Ensure that all food contact surfaces remain free of contaminants at all times. 

Multiple nozzles for the drive thru fountain drink machine were observed soiled during this inspection. Per the PIC they should be being cleaned every night as part of the closing procedure. This appears to not be happening. The PIC was shown a nozzle and instructed to clean them.  All of the nozzles were removed during this inspection and cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitize) to correct the violation.  The PIC should review cleaning procedures with the relevant staff to ensure that this is not an issue again.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. Ensure that all food contact surfaces remain free of contaminants at all times. 

1) Multiple nozzles for the drive thru fountain drink machine are observed soiled during this inspection. Per the PIC they should be being cleaned every night as part of the closing procedure. This appears to not be happening. The PIC was shown a nozzle and instructed to clean them.  All of the nozzles were removed during this inspection and cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitize) to correct the violation. 2) The inside of the ice chute in the customer area is observed with pink slime/green and black mold on the inside of the chute in cracks where the sides of the chute meet. The PIC was told and an employee instructed to clean with a sani rag to correct.  The PIC should review cleaning procedures with the relevant staff to ensure that this is not an issue again.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

During this inspection an employee was observed to probe multiple food items throughout the kitchen as part of their scheduled checks. As they were doing so they were only observed to wipe off the probe with paper towels. The probe should be sanitized between uses to ensure food safety is maintained. All items were within safe temperature ranges per inspector checks. The situation was discussed and education conducted with the PIC. Ensure that all items being used for multiple items and stored out of use for long periods of time between uses are sanitized between uses.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

What appears to be the remains of someone’s meal was observed on top of the in use soda syrups in the back of the facility. The PIC was shown and had the items removed to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all foods are consumed and stored so that contamination of foods or food contact items intended for consumers is not a concern.

findings.title: Allergen awareness notice
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.08(a). Food Allergy awareness. (a) A restaurant shall display a notice indicating to consumers that any information regarding food allergies must be communicated to an employee of the restaurant.

On arrival an allergen notice was not observed at the facility. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were unaware of one posted at the facility or on the menu. A notice given during this inspection to correct. Ensure that an allergen notice is observable by customers at all times.

findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) 

1) Multiple pans stored on the shelves as ready for use are observed with either baked on debris or greasy/oily residues. 2) A scoop is observed stored ready for use with a white stringy substance on the handle. The PIC was shown and moved the items to dish for re-cleaning. Education should be conducted with the dish washers to ensure that the dishes are always completely cleaned prior to storage and use.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the drive thru fountain drink machine are observed with significant filth build up on the inside of the nozzles. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean at all times. The nozzles were removed and washed during this inspection to correct the immediate violation.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

The shelf above the prep line has significant food debris and dust observed. This is where stacks of single service containers are stored prior to use out of their packaging. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean this location and maintain it clean moving forward to protect the food contact surfaces from contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

The metal sheet between the mop sink and the wall is pulling away from the wall under the faucets. This is exposing a gap that is not reasonably cleanable. The PIC is instructed to reseal the metal to the wall and ensure a smooth and easily cleanable surface moving forward.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

During this inspection the PIC could not show a CFPM certification to the inspector. Verification was available that the course was completed earlier this month but the certificate has not arrived/become available online at this time. No other employees currently at the facility have a CFPM certificate. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts and that copies of the certificates are available for observation at the facility at all times.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to handle a clean nozzle assembly for the fountain drink machine and install it with their bare hand and without hand washing. Breaking down boxes (that were on the floor) took place prior. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the nozzle replaced, taking care not to contaminate the item during installation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

1) There is a hole in the ceiling tiles in the dry storage area. Replace the damaged tile. The PIC indicated that this was were an old camera used to be. The tile should have been replaced at the time that the camera was removed. 2) The doors to the cabinets under the fountain drink machine in the customer seating area has two sections chipped away that expose the particle board. Repair or reseal so that there is a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 3) A hole is at shoulder level in the wall between the dry storage and walk-ins. Repair so that the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival none of the employees currently at this facility have a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certification. Per the current PIC, the GM walked out Saturday and took several managers with him. A remaining CFPM arrived during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

The bag of sanitizer concentrate used for filling the three part sink and bucket in the facility is observed empty at the beginning of this inspection. The bag was changed (the truck earlier today restocked it) and new buckets/ sink made in an attempt to correct the violation. After replacing the bag, the concentrations were still not coming out correctly on the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. At this time the solution is being manually made to reach the correct concentration for food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The ceiling tiles around the vents in the kitchen and prep areas have a significant amount of dust. PIC is instructed to clean often enough so as to maintain clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed sour cream in the bottom of the second line to be 52F. Also observed pico de gallo to be 50F in the top of the right side cold line. The line was shut down as the thermometer inside said 48F. It appears that the unit is freezing up. Ice can be seen under the plate. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) Pico and sour cream were discarded. Do not use the line until it is repaired. Or use 4 hour rule for time as a public health control. Time and date all foods on that side and use or discard in 4 hours.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Prep line on the drive up side (L) does not have a thermometer. The food is holding around 40F. Provide thermometers for all units. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: The bottom of the drive up side prep line is leaking. Sealed food bags were stored under this area but not under the water drips. The food was removed and bags were wiped down. Do not use this area for food storage until it is repaired. 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Doors on the hot holding box are cracked. Also, the seal on the stainless hot box top door is in disrepair. Replace doors and seal. 750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily clean able

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: Observed a coat to be hanging on a shelf holding food related items. Remove coat and store personal items properly. 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed both line cold holding units to have food above 46F when probed. Facility states that they have had issues with these units in the past. They stated they would start ice baths on all products on top of the table and keep no products in the below cooler until the units are repaired. 
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
750-280 Food handlers & consumers shall avoid direct hand contact with ready to eat foods.  When handling ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.).

Observed a small cup stored in a container of cinamon powder used for dessert items. Cup has no handle. Discussed and the cup was removed during the insepction.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the walk-in freezer to have an accumulation of ice within the walk-in freezer. Ensure the ice is removed and the walk-in is maintained in a smooth, easily cleanable. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed clean fryer equipment being stored on a shelf that was soiled with grease and food debris. Ensure clean equipment is stored on clean surfaces. 
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed cleaners being stored over a large bag of rice in the dry storage. Ensure that chemicals are stored below and away from food/food surfaces. Bottles moved during the inspection. 
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present

Observed no FSSMC present during the inspection. 1 FSSMC should be present during all hours of operation and prep. Ensure that additional FSSMCs are provided within the facility to cover all hours of prep and service. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed measuring cups used to scoop cheese being stored with the handle in the food. Ensure the food dispensing utensils are stored in one of the manners listed below. 
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee turn off the faucet without a barrier, after washing their hands. Ensure when turning off the faucet that a barrier is used to prevent recontamination. Employee was educated and instructed to rewash their hands. 
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
1) Observed personal employee items sitting over single service articles in a back storage area. 2) Observed a personal drink, open, being stored in the walk-in cooler above food for service. Ensure that personal items are stored below and away from products/food that are intended for service. Items moved during the inspection. 
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a leak from a condensation line in the walk-in freezer creating a significant amount of ice build up on the floor, as well as a stalactite-like formation of ice coming from the condensation line. Ensure that the ice is regularly scrapped away to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed a sanitizer bucket to not test for any sanitizer solution. Upon further investigation, it was noted that the sanitizer compartment of the 3 compartment sink also did not have any sanitizing solution. The manager noted the quat sanitizer product had ran out and replaced it. The sanitizer sink and bucket were remade during the inspection. Ensure that the sanitizers are tested daily before placing them into service. 
750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed 2 employees working within the facility, but neither of them to have an FSSMC. Facility has had past issues with having an FSSMC on at all times and being able to provide adequate documentation for FSSMC. The critical the last time it was given was closed due to the manager being able to show the national certificate, but not able to produce the IL license. The critical this time is being left open and a reinspection will occur in 90 days. Ensure that there are enough FSSMC on staff to cover all hours of food prep and service. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink next to the cash registers to have a hand soap dispenser that was inoperable. The machine appears to have dead batteries within it. Ensure that there is an adequate supply of hand soap, that is accessible, and hand towels at each hand washing sink. 
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed 10+ drain flies throughout the facility in the kitchen, dining room, bathrooms, and back storage area. Facility has been working with Orkin to foam drains and has increased cleaning. The facility should also avoid leaving standing water in places for long periods of time. The repair that will be made to the wall could significantly help the issue as well, since there is obvious water accumulation in the wall. The facility should continue increased pest control visits and cleaning to continue to decrease the drain fly population. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Rooms and equipment - vented as required
findings.comment:
Upon entering the facility this afternoon there was a thick accumulation of smoke noted throughout the air. The manager stated that a facility maintenance person had been out to the facility today to repair a belt on the ventilation system. Smoke was billowing out of the fryers and into the surrounding areas of the facility. The oil appeared to be dark in color, but the smoke was also not escaping through the ventilation systems. City of Springfield was contacted and 2 mechanical inspectors responded to the facility during the inspection. The mechanical inspectors stated that until the ventilation system was in complete repair, and could handle the smoke coming from the heating units under the hood, then the heating units should be shut down. Spoke with Mike, from franchise operations, during the inspection over the phone and he believed that the smoke was due to the fryer oil. Mike was advised that mechanical inspectors had inspected the unit and advised not to operate the equipment until Taco Bell's maintenance personnel could inspect/repair the equipment. Mike stated he was sending one of his maitenance men back to the facility to check the unit for proper operation. 
750-1250 All rooms shall have sufficient ventilation to keep them free of excessive, heat, steam, condensation, vapors, obnoxious odors, smoke, and fumes. Provide adequate ventilation.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed a non-toxic, non-stick spray can being stored on the chemical storage rack. Ensure that food and items used for food purposes are stored segregated from each other. Can was moved during the inspection by the manager. 
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed >50 drain flies throughout the facility. The infestation is extremely embedded into the facility. There were multiple stages of the drain fly life cycle noted when inspecting behind the shelving next to the service line. They were crawling in/out of cracks in the floor. Orkin has been out once since the initial inspection, but more frequent visits may be required until the infestation is eliminated. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the flooring and coving around the 3 compartment sink and behind the shelving on the service line to be excessively soiled and to have cracks in the tile and grout. The grouting by the service line is recessed to the point that water accumulation has started. The floors have food debris noted throughout the areas. The floors need to be repaired and thoroughly cleaned regularly. This with additional visits from pest control could help reduce the fly population. Areas where the coving is removed should be replaced, after ensuring the there is nothing wrong with the wall where the drain flies are most prevalent (divider wall between 3 compartment and shelving for service line). 
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility unable to produce IDPH licenses for FSSMC. There is no documented FSSMC in this facility at this time. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed the freezer to have a thermometer reading (-54F- (-67F)). This was not accurate. Ensure that if a thermometer is no longer working properly that it should be repaired, or a new one should be provided.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed a soiled pair of scissors being stored on a clean dish rack. Ensure that when utensils are soiled that they are placed through dish to be properly cleaned before being put away. Scissors were moved and placed in dish.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the cook line to have several items with measuring cups as the utensil with the handle resting in the food. This presents a  potential for cross contamination. Utensils should be stored in one of the manners listed below.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed the heating cabinet to be missing a handle. The cabinet is extremely difficult to open and is no longer smooth, easily cleanable in the areas where the handle broke off. 2) Observed the freezer to have an excessive accumulation of ice in the base. This no longer provides a smooth, easily cleanable surface. The ice should be removed or freezer defrosted. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean state. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed 20+ drain flies throughout the facility. Areas were they were seen include tortilla storage/hot cabinet areas on cook line, mop sink, dry storage in rear of facility, and dining room. This pest infestation appears to be well embedded within the facility and will require extensive treatments from the facility's pest control (Orkin), as well as extensive cleaning of the floors and drains in the areas mentioned above.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the back door self closer to be in disrepair. This was noted during the last inspection and a sign was allowed to be made stating to close the door tightly. Since the last inspection the sign has been removed. The back door should be provided with a self-closer that fully closes the door when opened. Ensure that the outer opening is repaired to close without assistance. 
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) Observed excessive accumulation of debris under the cook line and under the service counter. 2) Observed the drains in the cook line and by the soda machine to be soiled. These two items are both factors that would promote drain flies within the facility. All floors and drains should be thoroughly cleaned in an effort to decrease drain fly activity. This should be done in addition to contacting Orkin for further pest control treatments. 
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed chemicals (release agent) being stored above clean dishes in the bunn water heater area. Ensure that chemicals are stored below and away from food and food contact surfaces. Manager moved the chemical during the inspection. 
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed the facility's FSSMC on site to still not have valid proof of IDPH FSSMC. She attempted to speak with IDPH during the inspection, but was unable to obtain a duplicate copy. The FSSMC should be able to produce adequate documentation that shows they are licensed within the state of IL. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed a bag of soda syrup, out of it's box, but still connected to the machine, sitting on the floor. Employee was notified and bag was placed back in the box that was 6 inches off the ground.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed multiple employees leave their station and attend to tasks that were not on the food prep line. They did not remove their gloves, wash their hands, and don a new pair of gloves before returning to the food prep line to continue food handling. Ensure that proper practices are maintained when using gloves for food preparation. 
750-160bGloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda nozzles at the drive thru to have an accumulation of dried soda syrup. Ensure that food contact surfaces are regularly washed, rinsed, and sanitized.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed single service cup dispenser below the cash register that had an accumulation of food debris. The dispensers are no longer in operation due to them being in disrepair. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are maintained in good repair, as well as free of accumulation of dust, dirt, and debris.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed burrito wrappers and crunchwrap supreme wrappers that were being without any protection or protection over them. Ensure that single service articles are stored in a manner that prevents cross contamination. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the back door to the facility to have a self closer that was not fully closing the door. There was a significant gap following the use of the self closer and the door had to be manually pulled shut. The manager put a policy in place during inspection that the door should be manually, securely shut following each opening. A sign was hung on the door to inform employees to shut the door following use.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the back corner, unde the drive thru soda station, to have an accumulation of dirt and debris. Ensure that floors are maintained in good repair, as well as free of accumulation of dust, dirt, and debris.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed a hole in the wall in the back single service storage area. This hole is near the coving. Holes in walls and ceilings should be constructed so that they are smooth and easily cleanable. There was also the front hand sink counter by the drive thru window with caulking separating from the wall. Recaulk the hand sink counter where it is separating. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed a portion cup being used as a dispensing utensil in the bulk cinnamon container. Provide a dispensing utensil with a handle extending out of the food to eliminate potential for contamination.
750-280 To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees or provided to consumers who serve themselves..

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
REPEAT 1x> Observed the front hand sink to be slow draining. Provide properly draining fixtures.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels available at the front line handsink, however, employees were observed using the back hand sink throughout the inspection. Provide paper towels at all hand sinks.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 1) Observed the cove base tiles below the 3 pan sink to be detached and broken. Repair tiles to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 2) Observed the floor of the reach in freezer to have an accumulation of food debris. Clean and maintain this floor. 750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors. 750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ceiling tiles over the top of the make line equipment to have an accumulation of dust. Clean this ceiling to prevent possible contamination. These tiles are not directly over food preparation areas.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed multiple soiled and wet mops heads to be stored in the basin of the mop sink. Hang mops to ensure quick drying to prevent food/water sources for pest. 
750-1160 The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-140b Observed the date/time marking stickers for the squeeze bottles of sauces to not be properly documented. The labeling stickers indicated the incorrect discard time under the recording system that Taco Bell uses. The stickers for 10am on 4/21 were pulled and discarded during the inspection. The proper 8-Hour discard time for the squeeze bottles was added to the time system during the inspection. Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: 750-280 A portion cup is observed being used as a scoop within the bulk cinnamon and sugar container in the dry storage room. Cease use of the cup as a scoop. Provide a proper scoop with a handle that can be inserted out of the food. Grab the handle and not the edge of the cup. Food handlers & consumers shall avoid direct hand contact with ready to eat foods.  When handling ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.)

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1060 The frontline handsink has a slow drain. The drain would affect the ability to use this sink, however, most staff members are observed washing hands at the handsink on the south end of the building. The slow draining sink is located at the north end of the building.  All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 The following walls and attached equipment need cleaning attention: 1) the plumbing under the 3-part sink (grease and food debris); 2) floor of the walk-in cooler (around the legs of equipment); and 3) as you enter the walk-in cooler, look up and to the left. Over the top of the shelving is a manufacturers stickers that is peeling from the wall and has become coated with mold spores. Pull the sticker if you can or, if the sticker needs to stay in-place, make sure the back surface is bleached.  Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750.1210a Observed the light fixture above three part sink to have a leak. Repair light fixture and ceiling so that it does not leak.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. 
Observed a box of cinabon pastries in the walk in freezer that were open and not covered.
Properly store and protect food.
CORRECTED = Box was closed to correct violation and protect food from potential contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
Observed that the laminate on the right side door of the drink station in the dining room is separating from the door. 
Reattach laminate so as to be smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
Observed that the tiles around  the floor drain in the prep area have cracked, and the grout has worn away. Also the grout of the tiles at the drive through window wall is worn away. 
These were repaired after the inspection in January, but the repair did not last. Repair these tiles and grout so as to be durable in this moist environment.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
Observed the damp mop was not hung up between uses. 
Store damp mop hanging upright when not in use to promote air-drying to prevent mold growth.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed that the built in thermometers on the prep coolers on both prep lines were not functioning correctly.
findings.citation_text:
750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.
Place accurate thermometers in these units.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
The laminate on the cabinet next to the drive through is still loose. The owner has decided to remove laminate and paint surface underneath.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
Repair this equipment.
**REPEAT**

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed a box of drink cups stored on the floor in the break area. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
Store single-service items properly.
**Corrected= Cups were placed on a rack.**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The 1)grout around the floor drain, the 2)coving under the 3 part sink, and the 3)grout that is worn away in the tiles in front of the drink dispenser, have not been repaired as of yet. 
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
**REPEAT**
